notes_markdown:
### New

- **The sources panel can stay open.** Click the new pin at the top of
  the sources pane — or turn on **Settings → Sources → Keep the sources
  panel open** — and the pane stays docked beside the photos instead of
  closing every time you open a source. Switching folders no longer moves
  the photo sideways, a switch with the mouse is one click on a row, and
  switching from the Grid keeps the Grid. The keys stay with the photos
  until you press `S` (the row cursor and a light-blue edge show when
  they're in the pane); `Enter` opens a row and hands them back, `Esc`
  or `S` hand them back without opening anything. The pane steps aside
  by itself when the photo would get narrower than 560 px and in
  Compare, Survey, Match series, crop, sort mode and tethered sessions,
  and returns by itself. Off by default — nothing changes unless you
  pin. With the panel pinned, **File → Sources…** works in the Grid too
  and does what `S` does there: the keys move into the panel and the
  Grid stays (unpinned, the row stays greyed in the Grid). See the
  manual's Sources chapter.
- **Saved filters (`Cmd+F`).** Filters you set up once and get back with
  two keys. A saved filter combines what the filter keys can't say on
  their own — "four stars or better, not rejected, not developed yet",
  "85 mm from the last week", "everything undecided from the last
  fortnight". Get the view roughly right, press `Cmd+F` then `N`: the
  editor opens filled in from what you're looking at; add a condition,
  name it, press `Enter`. From then on `Cmd+F` and a digit shows it, on
  any folder or server. Eight things to filter on: flag, rating, colour
  label, edited or not, captured in the last N days / weeks / months,
  focal length, lens, camera. It behaves like every other filter — a
  photo that stops matching leaves the view, so a "not edited" filter
  empties as you develop — and `F` returns to all photos. The list shows
  each filter's live count; the rail's Filter palette and the `⋯` menu
  reach it with the mouse. In the batch panel, **This view (N)** is now
  offered whenever a saved filter (or a pivot) is on, so a batch acts on
  exactly the photos you see. Filters are kept in
  `~/.culler/filters.json`.
- **Manage a server's albums from culler.** Expand a server in the
  sources pane and a **+ New album** row leads its albums: `Enter`, type a
  name, `Enter` — the album is made on the server (a name that's empty or
  already taken is refused under the field). `R` on an album renames it,
  and `⌫` deletes an album you own that isn't shared: the row turns red
  and says what happens — the photos stay on the server, the album can't
  be brought back — and a second `⌫` deletes it (`Esc` stands it down).
  An album someone else owns shows their name after its own; `R` and `⌫`
  on it say whose it is instead of trying.
- **`Shift+I` files a whole selection.** With the photo you're on inside
  a selection, the album picker adds every selected photo in one go and
  says what the server did — "Filed 12 into 'Iceland' · 3 were already in
  it". Typing a name no album has offers **+ New album '…'** as the last
  row, so `Enter` on a partial match always files into the match; `Enter`
  on the new row makes the album with the photos in it. Inside an album,
  the picker's first row takes the photos back **out** of it (a
  selection asks once: "Space again removes 12 from …"), and they leave
  the view at once; a photo you can't remove — added to a shared album by
  someone else — stays, and the status line says so. The info panel's
  Albums section has an **Add to album… ⇧I** button.
- **Browse the open folder's subfolders from the sources pane.** With a
  folder source open, `→` on its row (or its chevron) lists the folders
  inside it — three levels deep, each with its photo count. `Enter` on
  one culls just that folder and the folders below it, with a strip
  above the photo saying which; `Esc` brings the whole source back with
  the cursor where you left it, and the batch panel offers the folder as
  **This view**. The counts are live: sort photos out of an Inbox and its
  number drops. The list comes from the photos culler already scanned,
  so drawing it reads nothing on disk — a folder you haven't opened
  never expands, and a folder with no photos in it doesn't show.
- **Make and rename folders from the sources pane.** Under the open
  folder — and under each folder you expand inside it — a **+ New
  folder** row makes a folder right there: `Enter`, type a name,
  `Enter`. `R` on a folder renames it on disk, then re-scans the source;
  if you were culling inside that folder you stay in it, on the same
  photo. A name that's empty, starts with a dot, or is already taken
  (in any mix of upper and lower case, where the disk ignores case) is
  refused under the field. A rename is also refused — saying why — for
  a folder that is a sort destination, a saved source, the export or
  tether folder, or holds one, and while a batch, a sort or a `J` is
  still running. `R` on the source's own row still renames its label in
  the list, never the folder.
- **Delete an empty folder from the sources pane.** `⌫` on a folder under
  the open folder arms it ("press ⌫ again to delete this empty folder"),
  a second `⌫` deletes it — only when there is nothing at all inside,
  checked on disk at that moment. A folder with photos in it, or anything
  else (another file, a subfolder, a hidden file), is never deleted: the
  status line says what is inside ("'Inbox' isn't empty — 212 photos.
  Move or trash them first."). `Esc` or any other key stands the arm
  down. A folder you sort empty stays in the list, so you can delete it.
- **Match Look is now Match series, and it opens on aligning your
  photos.** `M` still opens the session on the frozen set, but the panel
  beside the photos has two tabs. **Align** comes first: it says where
  the series stands ("6 points · 3 of 5 photos have them") and offers
  the next step as one button — and `Shift+C` now starts or continues
  the landmark walk straight from there, instead of needing `C` first.
  **Look** — one key away, `E` — is the tone-matching panel exactly as
  it was (Match, Reset all, the sliders). Under both tabs a line says
  what will be applied, next to **Done** (`M`) and **Discard** (`Esc`),
  so the whole job can be done with the mouse; the first `Esc` (or
  click) on a changed session turns Discard red and asks once before
  anything is thrown away. Aligning a series never touches its tone
  unless you open the Look tab and ask. Things that moved or changed
  name: `M`'s first screen is the Align tab (press `E` for the panel you
  knew); `E` and `L`/`Q` behave differently inside a session (`E`
  switches tabs, `L` and `Q` work on the Look tab); the photo's tag
  reads `[series]`; in a session's crop pass the button reads **Back to
  series** — and from the landmark view it now keeps the placement you
  just clicked instead of dropping it; an aligned photo's history entry
  reads "Aligned to" and the name of the photo it was aligned to.
- **"Edit landmarks" now edits them.** Once every photo in a series is
  aligned, the Align tab's **Edit landmarks** button (and `Shift+C`)
  opens the reference's points again — drag one to move it, click to add
  one, right-click to remove one — where it used to only say that
  everything was aligned. The other photos keep their points (they're
  paired by number), so `Enter` afterwards visits only a photo that an
  edit left with fewer than two, and Done saves just what changed.
- **Moving a reference point re-aligns the series.** After you edit the
  reference's landmark points, every photo whose crop is still exactly
  the one its landmarks gave it is re-aligned to the new points as soon
  as you're back at the series ("3 photos re-aligned to the edited
  landmarks") — `K` previews it, Done applies it, Discard takes it back.
  A photo whose crop you've adjusted by hand since keeps your crop ("1
  kept its hand-tuned crop"). Photos aligned before this version count
  as hand-tuned until you re-solve them once (`C`, `Shift+C`, `Enter`),
  because nothing recorded the crop their landmarks gave them.
- **Choose which tab Match series opens on.** Settings → **Match
  series** → **Match series opens on**: *Align* (the default) or *Look*.
  Every session starts on that tab; `E` still switches inside a session,
  and the next one starts on your choice again.
- **Uploads show how long they have run and about how long is left.**
  While a batch uploads to an Immich server, a line under the progress
  bar reads the elapsed time on the left ("1:50 elapsed") and an
  estimate on the right ("about 5 min left"). The estimate is worded
  coarsely on purpose, counts down, and corrects itself when the speed
  really changes — so it can go up. It stays blank for the first
  fifteen seconds, while a file has stopped moving and after Cancel,
  rather than show a number it can't stand behind. The corner pill's
  hover panel carries the same estimate; **Save edits to server** shows
  the elapsed time only. A batch that ran for ten seconds or more also
  says how long it took in its summary ("22 photos uploaded to prd in
  14 min").
- **Discard unsaved edits.** Changed your mind about a server photo's
  edits? A **Discard edits** entry now appears whenever a photo has
  unsaved edits — a **Discard** button in the develop pane's title row,
  the `⋯` menu, and the DEVELOP / CROP tab palettes — and reverts the
  whole photo (grade, crop, alignment, snapshots) to the last state you
  saved to the server in one click, with `Cmd+Z` bringing the grade and
  crop back if you change your mind again. The apply panel adds
  a matching **Discard unsaved edits** batch action to revert a whole
  scope at once (skipping, and naming, any photo it hasn't yet checked
  against the server). A photo you never saved reverts to the original.

### Changed

- **`J` on a photo you've only cropped now keeps the camera's look.** A
  photo with no grade — no develop slider moved; a crop on its own isn't
  a grade — exports (`J`, `Shift+J`, Export JPEG) and uploads to a server
  as its camera JPEG with your crop: the picture you saw while culling,
  instead of a flat render of the RAW. A photo you have graded still
  renders from the RAW, exactly as the develop panel shows it. When the
  bake isn't what's on screen — `J` with the develop panel showing the RAW
  of an ungraded photo, or re-rendering a server photo whose front is
  already a culler edit (which still comes from the RAW) — the status
  line says which file it used and why.
- **Landmark points alone no longer count as an unsaved server edit.** On
  an Immich source, the reference of a series you placed points on but
  never cropped or graded no longer shows in the "N unsaved" count,
  `Shift+U`, Save edits or the reminder on quit — saving it would only
  upload a new copy of an untouched photo. Its points stay in culler's
  state on this computer and travel to the server the next time that
  photo is saved with `J` for a crop or a grade.
- **Album changes on a server now report what the server actually
  did.** Putting a photo into an album or taking it out (`Shift+I`),
  uploading into an album, and `J` on a photo that lives in albums all
  used to treat any answer from the server as success. They now read the
  server's verdict per photo: a photo it refuses (someone else's photo
  in a shared album, for example) flips back in the album picker with
  "no permission", a photo that was in the album already reads "already
  in … — nothing added", and the upload summary counts the real adds —
  "· 2 added to 'Iceland', 1 already in it", or "· already in 'Iceland'"
  on a re-run — instead of always saying "added to".
- **A server key that lacks an album permission is told which one.**
  The message now reads "the API key lacks the albumAsset.delete
  permission — add it to the key in Immich" instead of "check the API
  key", and an album that was deleted in the meantime reads "that album
  no longer exists, or you don't have access to it" instead of "server
  returned 400". The manual's key-permission table now lists the album
  permissions, including the one for taking a photo out of an album that
  it was missing.
- **Album lists stay in step.** The sources pane, the Upload card and
  the album picker (`Shift+I`) each kept their own copy of a server's
  album list, and the picker's was fetched once per session. They now
  share one list that refreshes whenever culler changes an album: put a
  photo into an album and its count follows everywhere, with nothing to
  close or reopen.
- **A kept-open sources panel shows album changes made elsewhere.**
  When the keys come back to a pinned pane, or the window regains focus,
  the expanded servers' album lists refresh — an album made, renamed or
  deleted in the server's web app shows without a restart, and an open
  album renamed there takes its new name.
- **Trash inside an album says it acts on the server.** In an album
  view, choosing Delete to trash in the batch panel now reads "Trash
  deletes from the server, not just this album — ⇧I takes photos out of
  an album."
- **A source that finishes loading while the Grid is open now lands in
  the Grid** instead of waiting until you leave it. Before, pressing
  `K` while a server was still loading kept its final sort order and a
  large library's month list back until you left the Grid, and the scan
  warning's Retry sat on "Scanning…" there.
- **A source keeps its place when you only pass through it.** Opening a
  source and moving on to another before it had finished loading made it
  forget the photo and filter you had left it on. It now remembers them
  until you have actually been there again.

### Fixed

- **Switching source while a `J` is still uploading no longer puts the
  result in the wrong place.** A `J` (or "Save edits to server") that
  finished after you had opened another source could mark a photo of the
  source now on screen as the uploaded edit, and left the server you
  saved to still counting that photo as unsaved. The save now lands on
  the source it was started from, whatever is open when it finishes —
  including when you refresh that same source while it uploads.
- **Fixed:** opening Match series with the cursor on a photo that was already
  aligned to another photo, and leaving again, erased that photo's stored
  landmark points. A session that never touched a photo's landmarks now
  writes nothing for it.
- **Fixed:** holding `Esc` a moment too long inside a series session could back
  out of the landmark view, out of the crop pass, arm the discard and
  confirm it — throwing away the whole session from one press. Every
  `Esc` there now acts once per press, however long the key is held; the
  same goes for `M` (a held `M` no longer enters and immediately commits,
  or commits and re-enters) and for `Enter` in the landmark walk (a held
  `Enter` no longer accepts photo after photo). `Esc` on a value you are
  typing now only reverts that value; before, the same press also left
  the session or closed the crop pass.
- **Fixed:** in the landmark walk, `Tab` (skip a point) could leave the
  keyboard stuck until the next mouse click: a second `Tab` did nothing,
  and `Enter` jumped to another photo instead of accepting the one you
  were on. Skipping the last point and pressing `Enter` now accepts, as
  the walk always said it would.
- **Fixed:** pressing `R` (re-anchor) in a series session silently
  dropped the landmark points placed in that session — the reference's
  and every accepted photo's — so the following `M` saved the aligned
  crops with no points behind them. `R` is now refused while the session
  holds landmark work it would drop, and says how to keep it ("can't
  re-anchor — it would drop the landmark work on 2 photos · M commits it
  first"). Hand-aligned crops are unaffected and never block it.
- **Fixed:** `Esc` left a series session at once, with no "press Esc
  again", when the only thing you had changed was one photo's accepted
  landmark points (its crop came out the same). Those points are work
  `M` would have kept, so `Esc` now arms over them like any other
  aligned photo.
- **Fixed:** leaving a series with `M` said "committed — 0 photos
  updated" both when there was nothing to write and when it had written
  landmark points only. **Done** now says what it saved ("series done —
  6 landmarks and 2 photos aligned"), says "series closed — nothing
  changed" when there was nothing, and a discard names what it threw
  away.
- **Fixed:** the diagnostic log said `cancel: 0 develop + 0 crop writes`
  for every cancelled series session, whatever it threw away. A
  cancel now logs what it reverted — how many photos' tone and crop, how
  many photos' landmark points — and names each photo.
- **Paste no longer slips past a series' Done.** In a Match series
  session the Look tab's footer used to offer Copy and Paste, and a
  click on Paste wrote the photo's develop and crop to disk at once —
  even though nothing in a series is meant to be written until Done.
  Copy and Paste are gone from that footer, and `Shift+V` in a session
  now says why it does nothing; outside a session they work as before.
- **An album that can't be opened no longer marks its server as
  failing.** Opening an album that was deleted on the server used to
  turn the whole server's row to "Server error" until the next
  successful scan. The status line now says the album is gone, the row
  drops out of the list, and the server's row is left alone.
- **"MB left" during an upload no longer jumps back up** when a photo's
  RAW starts after its JPEG, and a photo that failed no longer leaves
  its unsent bytes in the count for the rest of the batch.
- **The upload speed graph's "up to N MB/s" caption no longer flickers**
  up and back down for a moment when a five-second bar completes.
- **Fixed:** in the sources pane, a stray `Shift+Tab` could move keyboard
  focus onto a row, after which the arrow keys did nothing and `Enter`
  opened the wrong source.
- **Fixed:** in the develop pane, the Auto button's label no longer
  collides with its `Shift+A` keycap when the look picker is on the row.
